title: CHAPTER TWELVE. Old Testament sacraments: circumcision and Passover
latin: CAPUT DUODECIMUM, De sacramentis veteris testamenti. Sacramenta V.T. sunt, quae populo Judaico a Deo tradita & instituta per rem terrenam Messiam venturum designabant ad conferendam et obsignandam Euangelii gratiam. II. Sunt autem potissimum duo, CIRCUMCISIO & PASCHA. Alia enim signa sub arctiore sacramentorum notione hic non censemus.
english: CHAPTER TWELVE. On the sacraments of the Old Testament.
Old Testament sacraments are those handed down and instituted by God for the Jewish people which through an earthly thing designated the coming Messiah for conferring and sealing Gospel grace.
II. There are chiefly two: CIRCUMCISION and the PASSOVER. Other signs we do not here count under the stricter notion of sacraments.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): II. There stand as chiefly two: CIRCUMCISION and ye PASSOVER. Other signs we do not here count under ye stricter notion belonging toward sacraments. — Old Testament sacraments stand as those handed down and instituted by God for ye Jewish people which through an earthly thing designated ye coming Messiah for conferring and sealing Gospel grace. — CHAPTER TWELVE. On ye sacraments belonging toward ye Old Testament.

title: III. Circumcision
latin: III. CIRCUMCISIO fuit sacramentum V.T. quo amputata pellicula praeputii pueruli octavo die a nativitate foedus Dei cum Abrahamo & semine eius obsignabatur, Gen. 17. Designabat circumcisionem cordis per Spiritum (Deut. 10:16; Rom. 2:28-29; Col. 2:11) & Christum in carne venturum. Octavus dies typum resurrectionis Christi & novi saeculi initium adumbravit.
english: III. CIRCUMCISION was an Old Testament sacrament by which, with the foreskin of the little boy cut off on the eighth day from birth, God's covenant with Abraham and his seed was sealed (Gen. 17).

It designated circumcision of the heart by the Spirit (Deut. 10:16; Rom. 2:28-29; Col. 2:11) and Christ coming in the flesh. The eighth day shadowed Christ's resurrection and the beginning of the new age.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): It designated circumcision belonging toward ye heart by ye Spirit (Deut. 10:16; Rom. 2:28-29; Col. 2:11) and Christ coming in ye flesh. Ye eighth day shadowed Christ's resurrection and ye beginning belonging toward ye new age. — III. CIRCUMCISION stood as an Old Testament sacrament by which, with ye foreskin belonging toward ye little boy cut off on ye eighth day from birth, God's covenant with Abraham and his seed stood as sealed (Gen. 17).

title: IV. Passover; Cap.13 next
latin: IV. PASCHA fuit agniculi immaculati mactatio & esus ad memoriam liberationis ex Aegypto & adumbrationem Christi. Agnus paschalis non est sacrificium proprie dictum, sed verum sacramentum adumbrans Christum eiusque meritum & beneficia credentibus conferens—quia in institutione nulla mentio sacrificandi; mactatio non a sacerdote sed a populo; non comburebatur sed comedebatur; mactabatur in Aegypto ubi nullum sacrificium offerri debuit (Exod. 8:26). Typus tamen sacrificii Christi: agnus anniculus immaculatus (1 Pet. 1:19; Isa. 53:9); segregatus; mactatus (Isa. 53:7); os non confractum (John 19:36); sanguis postibus adspersus; memoriale liberationis; caro edebatur sine fermento (1 Cor. 5:7-8). CAPUT DECIMUM TERTIUM sequitur, De baptismo.
english: IV. The PASSOVER was the slaughter and eating of an unblemished little lamb for memory of liberation from Egypt and as a shadow of Christ.

The paschal lamb is not a sacrifice properly so called, but a true sacrament shadowing Christ and His merit and benefits—because the institution mentions no sacrificing; slaughter was by the people not a priest; it was eaten not burned; and it was slain in Egypt where no sacrifice was to be offered (Exod. 8:26). Yet it was a type of Christ's sacrifice: unblemished yearling (1 Pet. 1:19); set apart; slain (Isa. 53:7); bones unbroken (John 19:36); blood on the doorposts; memorial of liberation; flesh eaten without leaven (1 Cor. 5:7-8).
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER THIRTEEN follows, On baptism. — Ye paschal lamb stands as not a sacrifice properly so called, but a true sacrament shadowing Christ and His merit and benefits—because ye institution mentions no sacrificing; slaughter stood as by ye people not a priest; it stood as eaten not burned; and it stood as slain in Egypt where no sacrifice stood as toward be offered (Exod. 8:26). Yet it stood as a type belonging toward Christ's sacrifice: unblemished yearling (1 Pet. 1:19); set apart; slain (Isa. 53:7); bones unbroken (John 19:36); blood on ye doorposts; memorial belonging toward liberation; flesh eaten without leaven (1 Cor. 5:7-8). — IV. Ye PASSOVER stood as ye slaughter and eating belonging toward an unblemished little lamb for memory belonging toward liberation from Egypt and as a shadow belonging toward Christ.
